problems: The flint bullet could say more plainly that python-flint 0.6–0.8 are no longer picked up automatically, which is the change most likely to surprise users.
The mpmath cap could arguably go under the same header instead of `other`. This is minor.
It leaves out two user-visible dependency changes: the supported python-flint versions changed (0.6–0.8 dropped, 0.10–0.12 added), and the install requirement now caps mpmath below 1.5.

But the PR also changes two things that do affect users. In sympy/external/gmpy.py, the python-flint versions SymPy uses automatically changed from 0.6–0.9 to 0.9–0.12. Any other version is used only when SYMPY_GROUND_TYPES=flint is set, and then with a warning. In pyproject.toml, mpmath is now capped at <1.5. Candidate A describes both changes accurately and briefly, so it is clearly better than leaving them out.

input.rationale: Most of this PR is CI and release-workflow work that users don't see, which is probably why Candidate B wrote NO ENTRY. But the PR also changes two things that do affect users. In sympy/external/gmpy.py, the python-flint versions SymPy uses automatically changed from 0.6–0.9 to 0.9–0.12. Any other version is used only when SYMPY_GROUND_TYPES=flint is set, and then with a warning. In pyproject.toml, mpmath is now capped at <1.5. Candidate A describes both changes accurately and briefly, so it is clearly better than leaving them out.
